LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 CORRELATIVE CONJUNCTIONS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words do we use when making a choice between two things?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text
2. use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication
3. use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 CORRELATIVE CONJUNCTIONS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 CORRELATIVE CONJUNCTIONS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions to a partner. (skill: use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text.
3. Practise this skill: use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication.
4. Practise this skill: use the pattern show... nominal... how/where/who in sentences.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words do we use when making a choice between two things?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Correlative Conjunctions means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify correlative conjunctions in an oral or written text.
5. Be able to: use correlative conjunctions correctly in oral and written communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
